test_meta.title: ST – Practice Set E: OR Safety, Environmental Controls & Legal Ethics

questions.stem: Which patient surgical position involves the patient lying flat on their back with legs abducted and elevated in padded stirrups, exposing the perineum for pelvic, rectal, or gynecological procedures?
questions.explanation: Lithotomy position places the patient supine with hips flexed and legs raised in padded stirrups. Both legs must be raised and lowered simultaneously by two staff members.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 10, pg 300

questions.stem: Why must both of the patient's legs be raised and lowered simultaneously and slowly by two surgical team members when placing a patient into or out of lithotomy stirrups?
options: To prevent sudden severe hypotension from rapid blood pooling and to avoid hip dislocation or lumbar torsional strain
To prevent contamination of the anesthesia circuit
questions.explanation: Lowering legs rapidly shifts 500-1000 mL of blood from the central torso into lower extremities, causing sudden cardiovascular collapse and dangerous hypotension.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 10, pg 301

questions.stem: Which nerve in the lower extremity is at high risk for compression palsy if the lateral knee or fibular head presses against metal lithotomy stirrup uprights without adequate gel padding?
questions.explanation: The common peroneal nerve wraps around the neck of the fibula; compression against unpadded stirrups produces foot drop (inability to dorsiflex the foot).
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 10, pg 302

questions.stem: In which surgical position is the operating table tilted head-down with the pelvis higher than the head, allowing gravity to shift abdominal viscera cephalad toward the diaphragm?
questions.explanation: Trendelenburg position tilts the head downward 15-30 degrees, shifting bowel out of the pelvis to improve visibility during lower abdominal and pelvic laparoscopic surgery.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 10, pg 298

questions.stem: What is the primary respiratory complication of prolonged steep Trendelenburg position?
options: Elevated diaphragmatic pressure causing reduced lung compliance, decreased tidal volume, and elevated intracranial/intraocular pressure
questions.explanation: Abdominal viscera push upward against the diaphragm in Trendelenburg position, reducing lung compliance and tidal volume while venous pooling elevates ICP and IOP.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 10, pg 299

questions.stem: Which position is standard for operative exposure during thyroidectomy, carotid endarterectomy, and laparoscopic cholecystectomy, where the table is tilted head-up and feet-down?
questions.explanation: Reverse Trendelenburg tilts the patient head-up, facilitating venous drainage from the neck/head and allowing gravity to pull abdominal viscera caudad for gallbladder exposure.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 10, pg 299

questions.stem: In the lateral decubitus position used for nephrectomy or thoracotomy, what soft supportive device must be placed under the dependent axilla to protect the brachial plexus from compression?
questions.explanation: An axillary roll is positioned just caudad to the dependent axilla on the lateral chest wall to relieve direct pressure on the brachial plexus and axillary vascular bundle.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 10, pg 304

questions.stem: When transferring an anesthetized patient from the operating table to the transport stretcher, who is in charge of directing the timing and movement of the transfer team?
options: The anesthesia care provider at the patient's head
The surgical technologist at the sterile field
The orderly at the foot of the bed
questions.explanation: The anesthesia provider maintains airway stability and cervical spine alignment at the patient's head and always calls the verbal count to initiate patient transfer.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 10, pg 296

questions.stem: What is the primary physiological mechanism that causes perioperative hypothermia in surgical patients under general anesthesia?
options: Anesthetic-induced inhibition of hypothalamic thermoregulation combined with vasodilation and cold laminar airflow in the OR
questions.explanation: General and regional anesthetics suppress the hypothalamus, preventing shivering and vasoconstriction. Peripheral vasodilation redistributes core heat to the cool body shell.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 10, pg 308

questions.stem: Which active warming system uses a motorized generator to blow temperature-controlled warmed air through disposable channeled blankets (e.g., Bair Hugger) to prevent hypothermia?
questions.explanation: Forced-air warming units (Bair Hugger) deliver convective heated air across the patient's cutaneous surface, representing the standard clinical defense against hypothermia.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 10, pg 309

questions.stem: What life-threatening pharmacogenetic skeletal muscle crisis is triggered by volatile inhalational anesthetics (sevoflurane, desflurane) or succinylcholine, requiring immediate administration of dantrolene sodium?
questions.explanation: Malignant hyperthermia is an inherited hypermetabolic disorder caused by uncontrolled calcium release in skeletal muscle. Dantrolene sodium (Ryanodex) is the specific intracellular calcium-channel blocker.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 9, pg 278

questions.stem: What is the earliest and most sensitive clinical sign of developing malignant hyperthermia in an anesthetized patient?
options: Unexplained rapid increase in end-tidal carbon dioxide (elevated ETCO2) and tachycardia
questions.explanation: Hypercapnia (elevated ETCO2) from hypermetabolism is the earliest sign of MH, occurring long before the dramatic late spike in body temperature.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 9, pg 280

questions.stem: What immediate action should the surgical team take if a drape fire breaks out on the patient in the operating room?
options: Immediately smother the flame with wet towels/saline, disconnect oxygen/breathing circuits, remove burning drapes from patient, and assess patient injury
Call the municipal fire department and evacuate the building immediately leaving the patient
Spray the patient's wound with dry chemical powder
questions.explanation: Immediate response: halt ventilation gases, extinguish flames with sterile water or saline, strip smoldering drapes off the patient to the floor, and maintain patient airway.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 4, pg 113

questions.stem: Which civil legal tort involves touching a patient without legal authorization or consent, such as performing a bilateral tubal ligation when consent was signed for appendectomy only?
questions.explanation: Battery is the intentional, non-consensual physical contact with another person. Performing an unconsented procedure or operating on the wrong site constitutes civil battery.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 2, pg 33

questions.stem: What legal term defines an act of omission (failing to do what a reasonable, prudent healthcare professional would do) or commission (doing what should not have been done)?
questions.explanation: Negligence is the departure from standard professional care that a reasonably prudent surgical technologist or nurse would exercise under similar circumstances.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 2, pg 32

questions.stem: What are the four mandatory legal elements that a plaintiff must prove to substantiate medical malpractice against a healthcare professional?
options: Duty of care, Breach of duty, Causation (proximate cause), and Damages (actual harm)
Contract, Fee payment, Negligence, and Discharge
questions.explanation: A malpractice lawsuit requires proving all four 'D's: Duty owed, Dereliction (breach) of duty, Direct proximate causation, and actual Damages suffered by the patient.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 2, pg 35

questions.stem: What is the primary objective of the Joint Commission Universal Protocol and pre-incision 'Time-Out' performed immediately before incision?
options: To verify correct patient identity, correct procedure, correct surgical site and side, and confirm prophylactic antibiotic administration
questions.explanation: The surgical 'Time-Out' ensures the entire surgical team pauses all activity immediately prior to skin incision to actively agree on patient identity, procedure, side, site, implants, and fire risk.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 10, pg 316

questions.stem: What standard counting sequence should the surgical technologist and circulating nurse follow when executing surgical counts?
options: Surgical field → Mayo stand → Back table → Off-field (kick buckets and trash)
Off-field → Back table → Mayo stand → Field
questions.explanation: Counts always follow a standardized spatial progression: closest to the patient wound (surgical field) → Mayo stand → back table → off-field kick buckets and sponge baggers.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 10, pg 313

questions.stem: What is the primary danger when laser energy strikes reflective, shiny stainless steel instruments in the surgical field?
options: Specular reflection of the beam diverting into adjacent tissues or personnel eyes, causing accidental retinal burns
questions.explanation: Specular reflection from shiny metal mirrors laser beams unpredictably into non-target patient organs or OR personnel eyes; black anodized (ebonized) instruments absorb beam reflections.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 4, pg 105

questions.stem: What color eyewear filter is required for surgical team members to protect their retinas when operating an Argon laser?
questions.explanation: Argon lasers emit visible blue-green light (488-514 nm); protective goggles must feature amber/orange optical density filters to block this wavelength.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 4, pg 105

questions.stem: Why are safety belts placed over the patient's thighs 2 inches proximal to the knees once the patient is positioned on the operating table?
options: To prevent the patient from falling off the narrow operating table during anesthesia induction, position changes, or emergence
questions.explanation: The safety strap is placed snugly over the thighs (2 inches above knees) with a two-finger space beneath to ensure the patient does not shift or fall from the table.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 10, pg 297

questions.stem: When using an ESU pencil near the head or neck during surgery under supplemental oxygen delivered via nasal cannula, what precaution must be strictly enforced?
options: Stop or reduce oxygen delivery during electrocautery activation and ensure no oxygen pocketing occurs under drapes
Use wet Ray-Tec sponges without water
questions.explanation: Oxygen pooling under drapes creates an oxygen-enriched atmosphere (>21%) that ignites explosively with a single spark from an active electrocautery pencil.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 4, pg 112

questions.stem: Which document must be readily available in the operating suite for every hazardous chemical used (such as formalin, glutaraldehyde, and bone cement) detailing emergency exposure and spill protocols?
questions.explanation: OSHA mandates that Safety Data Sheets (SDS, formerly MSDS) be immediately accessible to all employees for every hazardous chemical present in the facility.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 4, pg 107

questions.stem: In what container must surgical tissue specimens slated for routine permanent histology sections be preserved by the surgical technologist?
options: In a leakproof container submerged in 10% neutral buffered formalin
questions.explanation: Routine permanent pathology specimens are placed in 10% neutral buffered formalin solution (which fixes tissue proteins). Fresh frozen sections and stones are exceptions sent dry.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 10, pg 324

questions.stem: How should a tissue specimen intended for immediate intraoperative 'Frozen Section' diagnosis be sent to the pathology laboratory by the CST?
options: Sent immediately FRESH and DRY in a sterile specimen cup without any formalin or liquid fixative
questions.explanation: Frozen section specimens must be sent fresh and dry immediately so pathologists can freeze, slice, and stain the tissue within minutes without formalin artifact.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 10, pg 325

questions.stem: What is an event called that results in unanticipated death or serious physical or psychological injury to a patient (such as wrong-site surgery or retained foreign object)?
questions.explanation: The Joint Commission defines a Sentinel Event as an unexpected occurrence involving death or serious physical or psychological injury that signals the need for immediate investigation (root cause analysis).
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 2, pg 40

questions.stem: What is an 'advance directive' in medical legal ethics?
options: A legal document stating a patient's medical wishes and care choices in the event they become incapacitated (e.g., Living Will or Durable Power of Attorney)
questions.explanation: Advance directives are legal documents (such as living wills and durable powers of attorney for healthcare) that outline an individual's treatment preferences if they lose decision-making capacity.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 2, pg 43

questions.stem: Which agency regulates the efficacy and labeling of hospital disinfectants and chemical sterilants in the United States?
questions.explanation: The EPA evaluates and registers hospital disinfectants used on environmental surfaces to ensure antimicrobial claims and environmental safety.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 4, pg 97

questions.stem: What device is worn on the collar outside the lead apron by OR personnel to monitor cumulative monthly radiation exposure during fluoroscopy procedures?
questions.explanation: Personnel radiation dosimeters (film badges, TLDs, or OSLDs) monitor cumulative ionizing radiation doses to ensure occupational exposures remain below ALARA limits.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 4, pg 109

questions.stem: What term describes the professional obligation to maintain one's clinical competency through ongoing continuing education, certifications, and recertification cycles throughout one's surgical technology career?
questions.explanation: Continuing Professional Development (CPD) requires certified surgical technologists to earn continuing education credits (CEs) periodically to maintain NBSTSA active certification.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 1, pg 21
